claims.text: Medical image segmentation can degrade when one or more modalities contain imperfections; existing models may fail to detect these imperfections or dynamically adjust to data quality, particularly when test and training data differ substantially.

REDNet processes 3D volumes with separate modality-specific subjective logic networks, evaluates intra-modality consistency and cross-modality differences, discounts evidence at each pixel, and fuses it using Dempster–Shafer evidence theory.
ICEM compares evidence singular values with stored training-data singular values using the minimum class-normalized L1 distance, and combines this consistency metric with convolutional features.

CDAM constructs differential evidence between modalities and processes concatenated evidence through convolutional layers; larger discrepancies reduce the cross-modality weight and lead to greater discounting.

The discounting module combines intra-modality and cross-modality information, with both weighting hyperparameters set to 1, before merging discounted opinions using Reduced Dempster’s Combination Rule.
BraTS2021 contains 1251 scans with T1, T1Gd, T2 and FLAIR modalities; the study used 834 training, 208 validation and 209 test scans.

The Changhai Hospital dataset includes 139 patients with serous or mucinous cystic neoplasms, arterial, portal venous and delayed phases, and radiologist annotations of pancreas and tumor regions; the three phases were registered to the venous phase using Elastix.

Training used a learning rate of 1e-4 for 200 epochs, initial single-modality training followed by multi-modality training, and 128 × 128 × 128 crops. Evaluation used sliding windows with 0.6 overlap, Dice and HD95.

Models used the same dataset split, were selected using validation performance, and were evaluated without post-processing. REDNet reportedly outperformed other compared models on the in-house dataset, while slightly trailing the brain-tumor-focused CKD method in some BraTS measures.

In the reported Gaussian-noise experiments on both datasets, REDNet maintained the highest Dice and lowest HD95 among compared methods under noisy conditions; tested noise magnitudes were σ = {0, 0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 3.5}.
On BraTS with Rayleigh noise at scale 2 and synthetic intensity non-uniformity at magnitude 50, REDNet reportedly outperformed eight compared models across the standard BraTS evaluation metrics.
Under N-T1Gd corruption, the ICEM ablation model (Model3) achieved ET, TC and WT scores of 0.6955, 0.8107 and 0.9197, compared with reported baseline scores of 0.6760, 0.8027 and 0.9099.

The CDAM ablation model (Model4) achieved ET, TC and WT scores of 0.8521, 0.8961 and 0.9337, exceeding Models1–3 in the reported comparison, but slightly underperformed Model3 under N-T1Gd corruption.
For test images from uCT 960+ and iCT 256 scanners that differed from the training distribution, segmentation quality decreased, although the reported results remained anatomically consistent.
Always-on discounting reduces belief masses even for perfectly reliable inputs, slightly diminishing usable information from high-quality sources despite discount factors close to 1.

The study contributes a framework that dynamically calibrates modality influence at pixel level using ICEM, CDAM and discounting fusion, evaluated against conventional and uncertainty-based methods on BraTS2021 and an in-house pancreas dataset.
